faqs.question: Will I get a receipt?
faqs.answer:
Yes. An email receipt is sent at the time of your donation, to the address you enter on the donate page. If it hasn't arrived within a few minutes, check your spam folder before writing to us — receipts are sent by our payment processor and are sometimes filtered.

If your gifts total $250 or more in a calendar year, we also send a year-end acknowledgment letter for your tax records. You don't need to request it.

For a replacement receipt, or a receipt made out differently, email donations@nppc.org with the date and amount.

faqs.question: How do I cancel or change my recurring donation?
faqs.answer:
Email donations@nppc.org and we'll cancel or change it. Include the email address you donated with and the amount, so we can find the right subscription.

Monthly and yearly recurring gifts can be stopped at any time and there is no minimum commitment. Cancelling stops all future charges; it doesn't reverse a payment already taken. If a charge has just gone out and you'd like it back, say so and we'll refund it.

If you want to change the amount rather than stop giving, tell us the new figure — you don't need to cancel and start again.

faqs.question: Is my donation secure?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Card payments are processed by Stripe, and your card details are entered directly into Stripe's systems. They never pass through, and are never stored on, our servers — we don't have access to your card number.

What we do hold is what you tell us: your name, email address, and the amount and date of your gift. That is kept for our accounts and for sending receipts.

We don't sell, rent or trade donor information, and we don't publish donor lists. Given who this organisation works with, that matters more than it might elsewhere: if you would rather your support wasn't associated with your name at all, write to donations@nppc.org before giving and we'll tell you the options.

faqs.question: Where does my donation go?
faqs.answer:
Directly into prisoner support and the work that sustains it.

The largest share goes to material support for people inside and the people holding their families together: commissary deposits, travel costs so families can actually make visits, postage for legal mail, and re-entry assistance for the recently released. The rest keeps this archive and the site running — research, verification of case records, and the staff time behind them.

Our financials are reported in our Annual Report, which is the place to look for the breakdown rather than taking a summary's word for it.

We don't take money from law-enforcement organisations, prison contractors, or state agencies. Individual donations are what keeps that possible: every dollar from a supporter reduces our dependence on grant cycles and on funders who might prefer we were quieter.
